title: FreeMate Beginner Chess Course
description: A structured path from rules and piece movement through openings, blunder checks, and basic tactics.

categories.title: Rules of the Game
categories.description: Learn how the board works, how turns work, and how a chess game ends.

lessons.title: Name Every Square
lessons.summary: Use files and ranks to identify squares like d4, e5, and h8.
lessons.coachIntro: A chess coach always starts with the map. If you can name squares, every later lesson becomes easier.

steps.title: Files go up and down
steps.body: The letters a through h are files. They run vertically from White's side to Black's side.

steps.title: Ranks go side to side
steps.body: The numbers 1 through 8 are ranks. A square name combines a file and a rank.

steps.title: Find d4
steps.body: Trace the d-file and rank 4. Where they meet is d4.
tasks: Say the square name out loud

exercise.prompt: Before moving pieces, confirm you can name a square by file and rank.
tasks: Name the square where they meet

lessons.title: Checkmate vs Stalemate
lessons.summary: Understand the difference between a forced win and a drawn position.
lessons.coachIntro: Beginners often mix up checkmate and stalemate. This lesson gives you a simple ending checklist.

steps.title: Check means the king is attacked
steps.body: If your king is in check, your next move must remove that attack.

steps.title: Checkmate ends the game
steps.body: Checkmate happens when the king is attacked and there is no legal escape.

steps.title: Use the ending scan
steps.body: Ask these questions before deciding whether the game is over.
tasks: Can a piece block or capture?
Does the king have a legal move?
Can another piece block or capture?

categories.title: Piece Movement
categories.description: Practice how each piece moves and captures.

lessons.title: Move the Rook from d4
lessons.summary: Move the rook horizontally or vertically and avoid diagonal moves.
lessons.coachIntro: Rooks are powerful because they control long straight lines. You will see the legal squares, move the rook, then capture a target.

steps.title: Rooks move in straight lines
steps.body: A rook can move up, down, left, or right. It cannot move diagonally.

steps.title: Move to a legal square
steps.body: Choose any highlighted straight-line square from d4.
steps.successText: Nice. That is how a rook travels across a rank or file.

steps.title: Capture the hanging pawn
steps.body: Now capture the loose pawn on d7. The rook must move straight up the d-file.
steps.successText: Excellent. You used the rook's file to capture the hanging pawn.

exercise.prompt: Choose a destination square for the rook. The backend validates the move with python-chess.

lessons.title: Bishop Movement
lessons.summary: Learn how bishops travel diagonally and stay on one color.
lessons.coachIntro: Bishops and knights are both minor pieces, but their movement shapes are completely different.

steps.title: Bishops live on diagonals
steps.body: A bishop always stays on the same color square because it moves diagonally.

steps.title: Knights jump in an L
steps.body: A knight moves two squares in one direction and one square sideways. It can jump over pieces.

steps.title: Compare the shapes
steps.body: Use this quick comparison when deciding which piece can reach a square.

exercise.prompt: Compare the bishop and knight before choosing a move.
tasks: Knights jump in an L shape

lessons.title: Knight Movement
lessons.coachIntro: Knights feel strange at first because they are the only pieces that jump.

steps.title: Knights jump in an L
steps.body: Move two squares in one direction and one square sideways.

steps.title: Knight scan
steps.body: Check each possible L shape around the knight.

lessons.title: Queen Movement
lessons.summary: Combine rook lines and bishop diagonals.
lessons.coachIntro: The queen is powerful because she combines straight and diagonal movement.

steps.title: Queen equals rook plus bishop
steps.body: The queen moves along ranks, files, and diagonals.

steps.title: Queen line check
steps.body: Before moving the queen, check if the path is clear.

lessons.title: King Movement
lessons.summary: Move the king safely one square at a time.
lessons.coachIntro: The king is slow, but every move matters because the king can never move into check.

steps.title: One square only
steps.body: The king moves one square in any direction.

steps.title: Safety check
steps.body: A king move is legal only if the destination is safe.

lessons.title: Pawn Movement
lessons.summary: Learn pawn moves, captures, first moves, and promotion.
lessons.coachIntro: Pawns look simple, but their movement rules create many beginner mistakes.

steps.title: Pawns move forward
steps.body: A pawn moves forward one square, or two from its starting square if clear.

steps.title: Pawns capture diagonally
steps.body: Pawns do not capture the same way they move.

steps.title: Pawn rule scan
steps.body: Check the pawn rule before moving.

categories.title: Basic Opening Principles
categories.description: Build good habits in the first few moves of the game.

lessons.title: Choose a Legal First Move
lessons.summary: Practice common first moves that help control the center or develop a piece.
lessons.coachIntro: Openings are easier when you focus on goals instead of memorizing long move lists.

steps.title: Fight for the center
steps.body: Moves like e2e4 and d2d4 help your pieces reach important central squares.

steps.title: Develop before attacking
steps.body: Bring knights and bishops into the game before chasing tricks.

steps.title: Choose a legal first move
steps.body: Try e2e4, d2d4, c2c4, or g1f3.

exercise.prompt: Try a legal first move such as e2e4, d2d4, c2c4, or g1f3.

categories.title: Blunder Checks
categories.description: Pause before moving so you do not give away pieces for free.

lessons.title: Checks, Captures, Threats
lessons.summary: Use a quick scan before every move.
lessons.coachIntro: Most beginner games are decided by one-move mistakes. A short safety scan prevents many of them.

steps.title: Check forcing moves first
steps.body: Before moving, ask what checks your opponent has. Checks can change everything.

steps.title: Then scan captures
steps.body: Loose pieces are pieces that can be captured for free.

steps.title: The CCT scan
steps.body: Checks, captures, threats. This is your beginner blunder shield.

exercise.prompt: Before making a move, complete this safety scan.
tasks: What checks can my opponent make?
What captures can my opponent make?
What threat did my opponent create?

categories.title: Basic Tactics
categories.description: Recognize simple patterns that win material or create checkmate threats.

lessons.title: Spot the Fork Idea
lessons.summary: A fork attacks two valuable targets at the same time.
lessons.coachIntro: Tactics are patterns. You do not need magic vision, just a repeatable way to search.

steps.title: A fork attacks two targets
steps.body: A fork works because the opponent can usually save only one target.

steps.title: King forks are urgent
steps.body: If one target is the king, the opponent must answer the check.

steps.title: Fork search
steps.body: Use this scan when you are looking for a tactic.
tasks: Can one piece attack two targets?

exercise.prompt: Use this pattern check to look for a fork.
tasks: Can one piece attack two targets?
Can the opponent capture the forking piece?
